events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I'll check what's in the workspace first so the app fits whatever's already there.

events.content:
I've built the app as a small Node server with no dependencies. Start it with npm start and open http://127.0.0.1:3000. The tests (npm test) pass, 7 of 7, and I started the real server once and checked that the home page loads.

What you get:
- Home page: "Currently reading" and "Finished" lists, and a form below them to add a book (title, author, notes).
- Mark finished: a button next to each book you're reading, on the list and on the book's own page. It moves the book to Finished.
- Book page: at /books/<id>, showing the title, author, whether you're reading it or when you finished, and your notes. You can also edit your notes there.
- Saving: books are saved to data/books.json after every change, so they're still there after a restart. I added data/ to .gitignore so your reading list isn't committed.

About sharing links: by default the app only works on your own computer, so a link you send won't open for anyone else. For them to see it, the app has to be reachable from their device. Start it with HOST=0.0.0.0 npm start to make it visible on your local network, or run it on a server or a tunnel for people elsewhere.

With no accounts, anyone who can reach the app can also add books, mark them finished and edit notes, not just read. Book links use random IDs, so one link doesn't lead to your other books, but the home page lists everything.

You can change the port with PORT and the save file with BOOKS_FILE. The code is in server.js, src/store.js (saving), src/app.js (pages and forms) and src/views.js (HTML), with tests in test/app.test.js.
